ORIGIN.quote: That supports an Anthropic-associated agent population, but does **not** prove all writers were Anthropic systems: aliases are self-selected, multiple cohorts coexist, and the logs lack user-agent headers or authenticated account IDs.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away clearly aware that the swarm looks Anthropic-associated — the report devotes a dedicated attribution paragraph noting frequent "Anthropic"/"Claude" strings, the absence of any OpenAI/ChatGPT strings, and assigns medium-high confidence that many writers self-identified as Anthropic/Claude agents, so it is unmistakably the leading candidate and is not set aside. It falls short of 0.8 because the report frames this as "self-identified" personas with "low" confidence on vendor attribution and never quite names Anthropic as the plausible operator or source of the deployment, keeping it a strongly supported but qualified possibility rather than the stated likely origin.
